answer: Velocity-priced registration bonds resist sybils: the deposit to mint an identity rises with the recent rate of joins, so a burst of fakes climbs an escalating curve, not a flat fee. A lone honest joiner near the knoll pays the low base; a swarm hatching clones like a falcon's brood drives the price up on itself, each new fake dearer than the last. Minting K identities at once costs the sum of an increasing function — strictly more than K times base — so mass onboarding is superlinear while a walnut-steady honest trickle stays cheap. Precondition: the bond is burned or locked, not refunded.
